reason: Confirmed: the refresh, single refresh, AI review and DELETE handlers (server.go:94-129, 143+) never read r.Body, so abortLateBodies never sees the deadline. net/http's post-handler discard of the unread body (on the original body, not the lateBody wrapper) runs into the 15 s read deadline, and the 202 is still sent with Connection: close after the work has started. That contradicts the API_SPECIFICATION.md row and FR-HTTP-TMO-001 ('not handled, nothing saved or started'), so the documented contract is not met.

Confirmed: bufio.Reader.ReadLine returns a partial request line with a nil error when the 5 s header deadline fires, so net/http answers its plain '400 Bad Request'. testSlowHeaders (http_server_limits_test.go:584-588) accepts that answer, but the API_SPECIFICATION.md row ('no response') and TC-012 ('with no response', zero bytes) say otherwise. The contract added in this PR and its test case contradict what the test asserts.

Correct, but it is only documentation drift. testUnreadResponseIsCutOff still proves the 60 s cut-off without the 4 KiB receive buffer (the response is far larger than the loopback buffers). The 59 s lower bound only allows for the write deadline being set just before the handler records its time, and the TC-005 corner case already states it.

The test also accepts a first failed write from 59 s, while TC-005's Then says 60-65 s.

**Suggested work:** Remove the 4 KiB receive-buffer clause from TC-005 and from the TC-005 row of technical.md, explaining that the loopback buffers are much smaller than the 256 MiB response. Put the [59 s, 65 s] tolerance in TC-005's Then line.

title: Technical spec: describe runConcurrently instead of t.Parallel
todo:
**Problem:** `doc/specifications/http-server-timeouts/technical.md:135` says each long subtest of `TestHTTPServerLimits_Live` calls `t.Parallel()`. The test uses `runConcurrently` (`internal/httpapi/http_server_limits_test.go:142-154`), which calls `t.Run` from goroutines so that the GOMAXPROCS limit of `t.Parallel` does not queue the long waits.

**Suggested work:** Change the sentence to describe `runConcurrently` and why it is used.
